questions.q: What were the plant workers trying to find out with the safety test?
a: Whether the reactor could power itself while backup generators started
Whether the control rods could be removed without any risk
How long the plant could run without cooling water
Whether the roof could withstand a steam explosion
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains the test was meant to show the reactor could supply its own power during the 45-second gap before backup power.

questions.q: Why were the backup generators a concern during the test?
a: They took 45 seconds to restore power, which was dangerously long
They had never been tested before the accident
They ran on a fuel the plant did not have in stock
They could only power the control room
questions.why: The summary says the 45 seconds needed to bring backup power online was considered dangerously long.

questions.q: What design flaw made the emergency shutdown so dangerous?
a: The control rods had graphite tips that boosted power instead of cutting it
The rods were made of uranium and kept the reaction going
The cooling water turned into graphite under intense heat
The shutdown button was wired to the wrong pump
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that the RBMK reactor's graphite-tipped rods increased reactivity when inserted into the already unstable core.

questions.q: What role did Dyatlov play in the disaster?
a: He dismissed the crew's doubts and pushed them to keep going
He ordered the test cancelled twice before midnight
He warned Moscow about the reactor's design flaw
He refused to let the night crew begin the test
questions.why: The summary describes Dyatlov as an arrogant leader who scolded the crew for asking questions and ignored their uncertainty.

questions.q: Why was the official response to the explosion so slow?
a: Officials denied the reactor was damaged and understated radiation levels
The fire department refused to enter the building
The plant had no telephone line to Kyiv
Residents were evacuated before anyone reported the fire
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the director reported only a damaged hall and ignored a worker's far higher radiation reading, delaying help.
